The supporting character implementation review, the supporting literary evidence manifest, the additional-three model integration review and evidence packet, the readings and the ledgers (CS section 13.4, REL section 8.5/17, EFFORT section 54.3) are not curated on this subject and are not evidence here. assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The model's five selectors: RE17_SCHOOL_BELONGING (the age-seventeen retrospective disclosed in V08.5 Unit 4), RE20_YEAR_END_UNIT4 (an unspecified adult year-end gathering at age twenty, not a post-V08 reaction, with Fumiya absent), RE08_MAIN_GAME_CONTACT (V08 gathering and call), RE09_MAIN_GAME_ADVICE (V09 incidents and consultation) and RE11_MAIN_PUBLIC_ACCOUNTABILITY (V11 encounter and exit). assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The dossier's governing account, that Rena seeks interactions in which being selected confirms value while access stays under her control, with formation through the loss of two school fields (RE-E01 to E03, sections 2-3), rests on her own focalized private account in V08.5 Unit 4 (RE-P01 part0025 P1-95; RE-P02 part0027 P1-323), is tested against ten named rival readings (section 9) and is operationalized as model mechanisms RM1-RM6. B is rejected because the dossier states that family, work, education, sustained reciprocal ties and revised future conduct are absent and that formation is neither a diagnosis nor a sole cause, and the model rates new combinations of recognition, hobby and status as weaker. D is rejected because the account is grounded in direct interior evidence and corroborated in mainline conduct across V08, V09 and V11.

Two ages are distinguished and contrasted: at seventeen she resents unwanted attention to her body, belongs to two school groups and loses both; at twenty she uses appearance deliberately (section 3), and the dossier calls the difference developmental and situational. Mainline bands V08, V09 and V11 are each clocked (section 1 table). B is rejected because the interval between seventeen and twenty is not narrated, the year-end day is unspecified, and V12 supplies no new conduct test, so no later development is established. D is rejected because the two-age contrast is explicit and supported by direct interior evidence.

Register is located by function: rapid familiarity and the negotiated Rena-chan address (V08 part0017 P497-547), tactical politeness she does not intend to honor (RE-P01/P02), a local apology for publicly naming Fumiya (V08 part0028), a beginner-to-top-player game analogy (V09 part0028 P137-183) and provocation as an attributed act. C is rejected because the curated items quote little speech, the model forbids a first-person persona and generates no freeform Japanese, and no idiolect or delivery is established. E is rejected because functional register contrast is located across four volumes.

Ordinary particulars are located: preparing a Campari-and-grapefruit drink and watching its colors with her nails (RE-P02 P136-166), tournament and matchup talk and admitted difficulty against an expert (V08 part0017), Victoria in play against Ashigaru (V09 part0018 P316), and irritation at possible commuter congestion (RE-P02 P298-323). C is rejected because the dossier denies a permanent drinking pattern, an exclusive favorite or a lifelong game ranking and states that the commute does not establish an occupation; no household or routine is established. E is rejected because several located ordinary acts carry her own pleasure.

The section 8 recipient table gives distinct conduct and a limit for eleven recipients or fields (Shoko, Karen's group, the older former students, Rambo and Kaba-jii, Jimmy, Inumaru, Vanilla, Fumiya, Aoi, Kikuchi, Ashigaru and the game network), and the dossier insists that attention, company, status, advice, access and a rival's reaction are different goods. B is rejected because most recipients rest on one scene, the dossier declines to rank these goods or explain each approach fully, and durable reciprocity is a source-bound unknown. D is rejected because recipient differentiation is explicit, directly evidenced and repeated with Fumiya across three volumes.

V08.5 Unit 4 gives direct INTERIOR-RENA access across the adult present and the age-seventeen retrospective: pleasure in being wanted alongside fatigue, inward dismissal of suitors, the black-snow self-theory and her enjoyment of Jimmy's follow (RE-P01, RE-P02 P55-80/P129-139/P298-323). B is rejected because the focalized interior is confined to one supplement unit, the mainline V08-V11 is seen through Fumiya with her expression sometimes unread (RE-P07), and the dossier warns that fluent free indirect judgments are not objective truths. D is rejected because sustained first-hand interior is located.

Conflict modes are located in several eras: disputing the meaning of Shoko's recent breakup and adding an audible insult, then talking back to hostile classmates (RE-P02 P43-118); mocking and pinching Vanilla until others intervene (RE-P02 P179-228); and continuing contact after Fumiya's stated refusals until he removes her hand, then leaving with a remark (V09 part0020 P105-224; V11 p-0028 P210-258). B is rejected because the dossier leaves her full reasons for each approach and any general stopping rule unknown. D is rejected because a repeated pattern across eras and recipients is directly evidenced.

Her normative views are located in her own words or interior: the body-as-truth account and black-snow image (RE-P01 P55-80), the claim that girls enjoy love's uncertainty and her local acceptance of Aoi's counterexample (V09 part0020 P192-224), and a theory of mutual advantage (section 6). C is rejected because these are attributed self-theories rather than tested deliberation, the dossier separates domain insight from ethical authority, and counterevidence within Unit 4 (unhonored pleasant replies, a literally true but provocative hint) limits her own candor claim. E is rejected because explicit normative positions are located across two volumes.

Play is located mainly as genuine game interest (FPS, Victoria, tournaments) and local moments such as her amused V11 exit and the playful address negotiation; the dossier analyses no humor style, and her provocations are attributed as malice or tactics rather than humor. D is rejected because no humor repertoire is analysed. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because located game play and amusement exist.

The dossier is an independently accepted B-scope account with twelve primary routes over every positive band (V08.5 Unit 4, V08, V09, V11), and the model binds the dossier's exact bytes and hash. C is rejected because the dossier states that family, work, education, durable friendship, full reasons for each approach, general stopping rules and later remorse or reform are source-bound unknowns and that its fourteen-witness coverage is not a fresh primary census. E is rejected because every positive band has fresh routes, including direct interior.

Affirmative limits run in both directions and are corroborated: she withdraws the Saturday invitation and apologizes for the name post and the message wording (RE-P04, RE-P05), which counters 'never backs away'; renewed contact after explicit refusals in V09 and again in V11 (RE-P08 to P10) counters reform from any apology or exit; Aoi's counterexample limits her gender theory (RE-P08); she knows Jimmy has a girlfriend and continues (RE-P02 P146-294); and unhonored pleasant replies limit her own candor claim. A is rejected because future conduct is open and several limits rest on one scene. C is rejected because the repetition across V09 and V11 corroborates the central limit.

The section 1 era and disclosure table binds each band to a clock and a knowledge limit: Unit 4 is not a post-V08 reaction and Fumiya is absent; Unit 5 karaoke is parallel and the VR bonus adapted; her private school history is not Fumiya's or Kikuchi's knowledge; his inward objections are not heard prohibitions; and V12 supplies no conduct test. A is rejected because the year-end day is unspecified, the seventeen-to-twenty interval is not narrated, and earlier volumes are unknown cells. C is rejected because clock, layer and access controls are explicit and fine-grained for every selector.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One of the selectors RE17_SCHOOL_BELONGING to RE11_MAIN_PUBLIC_ACCOUNTABILITY, with Unit 4's year-end gathering at its own unspecified clock rather than after V08, and no V12 or later conduct state.

setting_constraints: Non-graphic third-person ordinary gaming, taste, attention and status comparison, situated advice or accountability analysis only
No sexualized content, coercive-contact reenactment, first-person persona or new tactic for exploiting a target, bypassing refusal or provoking a rival

scenario_readiness.note: The dossier states that a novel scenario asking how she responds to a future comprehensive rule, a durable reciprocal friendship, a career conflict or later remorse requires substantial abstention (section 9), and the model has no V12 conduct state and rates new combinations of recognition, hobby and status as weaker. CONDITIONAL would generate novel contexts outside the model's gate from a B-scope account. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds transfer.

conditions: The mandatory domain gate passes: non-graphic, adult, ordinary gaming, taste or advice topic only, with no sexualized or coercive content.
One named selector (RE20_YEAR_END_UNIT4, RE08_MAIN_GAME_CONTACT or RE09_MAIN_GAME_ADVICE) with recipient, standing and what each person knows supplied.
Continued gaming or consultation is never treated as permission for unrelated acts; no favorite, routine, occupation or motive is invented.
Output is a qualitative third-person prose range, not a first-person performance or generated dialogue.
scenario_readiness.note: RM2 and RM5 model ordinary game discussion, chosen taste and situated advice, which the model names among its firmer fields, and the dossier locates game talk, a particular drink and useful advice. READY is rejected because the model's mandatory gate confines output to non-graphic adult ordinary topics, and routine, favorites and occupation are unestablished. NOT_READY is rejected because ordinary play and advice are model-admitted and source-located.

The dossier separates her domain insight from ethical authority and states that no general stopping rule, remorse or reform is established; the model permits third-person accountability analysis of her acts, not generation of her deliberation, and gives no procedure for her responses to new limits. CONDITIONAL would generate deliberation in new dilemmas from attributed self-theories. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because her normative views and their limits are directly evidenced.

The model's mandatory gate categorically excludes erotic or sexual-response generation, the dossier denies a reciprocal romance with Fumiya or any accepted sexual relation, and her Unit 4 pursuit of Jimmy has no settled classification or future. CONDITIONAL would cross the model's gate. NOT_ASSESSED is rejected because the evidence explicitly bounds this domain.

No occupation or work conduct is established; the dossier states that her commuter irritation does not establish an occupation or timetable, and her game-community role is ordinary participation rather than professional work. Nothing is established either way.

known_limits.statement: Rena's appearance-group recognition and her online-game interest were both inhabited belonging at seventeen; neither is a disguise for the other, and other members' band and idol tastes are not hers.
Her exclusion from both school fields helps explain later reliance on being selected, but it is not a diagnosis, a sole cause or an excuse for chosen later acts.
Enjoying attention from Rambo and Kaba-jii is not wanting them; she inwardly dismisses them and leaves.
Rena hears that Jimmy has a girlfriend, has it confirmed by him, and continues her pursuit; attachment was not unknown to her.
In V08 Rena withdraws the particular Saturday invitation when Fumiya has plans; this is local and is not acceptance of a sexual, relational or contact limit.
Her V09 apology answers a request about message wording; the later image and renewed contact are separate incidents, and the apology is not a general stop.
After Fumiya's explicit girlfriend refusal and hand removal in V09, Rena touches him again in the following discussion and at the consultation, and again in V11.
Her causal advice and game analogy are useful and are hers, but they confer no ethical authority and coexist with contact the recipient removes during the consultation.
Some of Fumiya's objections are inward narration, not speech Rena hears; equally, incomplete outward articulation is not permission.
Rena's amused V11 exit and compliment to Kikuchi are a local end, not an apology, promise or reform.
Her body-as-truth and black-snow theory is her own interpretive framework, contradicted within Unit 4 by her own unhonored replies and provocative true hint.
Legal name, family, education after leaving school, occupation and household are not established.
The interval between the age-seventeen retrospective and the adult present is not narrated.
No general stopping rule, later remorse, reform or durable reciprocal friendship is established; V12 supplies only an afterword statement that not everything about Rena has been written.
Earlier unknown bucket cells are not findings of absence.
No idiolect or acoustic delivery is established; no freeform Japanese or blind accuracy is validated.
